title: Occupancy-Quantile Eviction and Fused-Arena Profiles (design sketch)
body:
Summary:

This is a working sketch proposing an occupancy-quantile driven eviction policy combined with an arena fusion profile for the KV cache. The goal is to reduce fragmentation across heterogeneous workloads, improve tail latency under memory pressure, and provide predictable tenant-level retention behavior while enabling low-cost background compaction.

Key objectives:
- Keep per-tenant hit rate degradation under 5% after eviction-trigger events.
- Bound worst-case eviction latency to avoid long blocking pauses on the serving thread.
- Reduce inter-arena fragmentation by at least 30% in mixed short/long-sequence workloads relative to the current slab-only allocator.
- Provide observability surfaces for occupancy quantiles and compaction debt.

Motivation / Observed problems:
- Slab fragmentation: workloads with highly skewed key sizes and short-lived sequences leave many partially used slabs, causing overall capacity loss.
- Tenant imbalance: aggressive tenant traffic bursts lead to eviction storms that unfairly evict high-value prefixes.
- Compaction interference: synchronous compaction during eviction spikes causes tail latency spikes.

High-level design:
1) Occupancy quantiles: maintain lightweight per-arena/tenant occupancy histograms (approximate quantiles) at 1%, 10%, 50%, 90%, 99%. These drive both admission and eviction decisions. Quantiles are updated via asynchronous samplers to avoid hot paths.

2) Quantile-aware admission: incoming items are admitted into a target arena based on predicted future occupancy percentile. If the predicted 90th percentile for an arena exceeds a tenant-configured soft-limit, we either route to a fused arena (see below) or apply an admission throttle for low-priority tenants.

3) Fused arena profiles: instead of a single slab size per arena we allow a fused arena to contain multiple micro-slab classes (e.g., 64B, 256B, 1KB) co-located with a small metadata bitmap mapping. Fusion reduces cross-class fragmentation and makes compaction more effective because hot micro-slots can be relocated within the same arena without cross-arena copy. Fused arenas are allocated on-demand and prefer NUMA-local memory.

4) Quantile-driven eviction rules:
- Evict from the lowest ROI cohort until target occupancy quantile is achieved (e.g., drive 90th percentile occupancy to below tenant soft-limit).
- Avoid full-scan tail-chasing: eviction candidate selection uses a combination of frequency sketch + recency buckets and weights them by occupancy quantile.
- Use a budgeted async reclaimer thread to perform non-critical evictions and compactions; synchronous eviction only reclaims a small deterministic headroom (e.g., 4% of arena) to satisfy immediate allocation needs.

5) Compaction debt and pacing:
- Track compaction debt per arena: bytes that could be reclaimed by compaction but currently blocked by in-use items.
- When debt > threshold, schedule short-window compaction jobs during observed low-p95 CPU or network usage. Compaction carries a cost accounting tag tied to tenant metrics so compaction load can be billed/back-pressured.

Data structures (sketch):
- ArenaDescriptor: id, numa_node, fused_profile_id, occupancy_quantiles[5], compaction_debt_bytes, active_count, free_segments_count (stored in cacheline-friendly layout).
- MicroSlotMap: per-fused-arena compact bitmap mapping micro-slot -> entry header offset (approx 1 bit per micro-slot + sparse index for large runs).
- FrequencySketch: small count-min sketch per-arena for hotness estimation (bounded 32KB).
- EvictionQueue: lock-free per-arena ring where candidates are pushed by allocation failures and async samplers.

Eviction flow (runtime):
1) Allocation attempts in arena A fail to find contiguous micro-slots. Blame is recorded to EvictionQueue(A).
2) Synchronous fast-evict: evict up to N_headroom entries using deterministic low-overhead policy (LRU-ish buckets) to satisfy immediate allocation. N_headroom tuned to avoid long stalls.
3) If still insufficient, escalate to the async reclaimer which uses occupancy quantile target to decide how many bytes to reclaim from A. Async reclaimer scores candidates by (frequency, recency, size, compaction-benefit) and issues batched removals and optionally in-arena relocation to reduce fragmentation.

Fragmentation mitigation techniques:
- Micro-slot packing: when relocating an entry during compaction, prefer moving into existing micro-gaps to avoid creating new externally-fragmented regions.
- Small-object clustering: co-locate short-lived short sequences into dedicated fused arenas to contain churn.
- Cross-arena consolidation: periodically (low priority) identify arenas where free ratio < X% but many small free runs exist and consolidate live entries into a new arena to free contiguous regions for large items.
- Adaptive slab morphing: fused arena can change micro-slab ratios over time based on observed size distribution (e.g., increase 64B fraction if >70% incoming items are <=64B).

NUMA and placement policy:
- Allocate fused arenas on the NUMA node of the requesting worker whenever possible.
- Allow controlled overcommit across NUMA nodes for low-priority tenants to utilize spare capacity while honoring soft isolation for premium tenants.

Observability and telemetry:
- Expose per-arena occupancy quantiles as time-series with 10s resolution.
- Track compaction_debt_bytes, compaction_run_duration, reclaimed_bytes, and relocation_count.
- Eviction.log structured events: reason, arena_id, tenant, reclaimed_bytes, latency_ms, candidates_scored.

Microbench experiment plan (quick summary):
- Workloads: mix A (high short-lived traffic), mix B (long context reuse), mix C (mixed small+large keys with bursts).
- Baseline: current slab allocator + LRU.
- Variants to test: fused arenas (no compaction), fused + async compaction, fused + quantile admission, full stack.
- Metrics: effective capacity (hit rate at fixed memory), tail latency p99 allocation latency, fragmentation ratio (free_bytes / reserved_bytes), compaction CPU cost.
- Preliminary results (synthetic, run 2024-09-25): fused+async compaction reduced fragmentation ratio 34% vs baseline and improved p99 allocation latency by ~15% under Mix C at 80% occupancy. CPU overhead for compaction was ~2.6% of serving CPU in the test cluster. Need real-world traces to validate.

Rollout plan (phased):
- Canary: enable fused arenas for low-priority tenants in dev region for 2 weeks, collect quantiles and compaction impacts.
- Beta: enable for 10% of tenants with opt-in flags and elevated observability.
- GA: auto-tune fused profile and enable for all unless tenant requests strict slab-only policy.

Open questions / considerations:
- How to price compaction CPU to tenants with variable SLAs? (billing vs throttling)
- Safety bounds for in-arena relocation under concurrent readers — need RCU-style epoch guarantees or per-entry pin counters.
- Worst-case memory blowup while consolidating arenas (need temporary reservation strategy).
- Interactions with persistent KV snapshotting and warm-up semantics (relocating entries changes physical layout; ensure snapshot consistency).

Todos (next steps):
- Prototype MicroSlotMap and fused arena allocator (owner: Liang).
- Implement occupancy quantile sampler using reservoir sampling or t-digest approximation (owner: Ethan).
- Add compaction debt metrics to existing telemetry pipeline (owner: Priya).
- Run renewed traces from production for Mix C replication (owner: Marina).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally a working sketch; I expect pushback on complexity vs benefit. Focus review on the eviction budgeting and compaction safety model.
- If we accept fused arenas, we should add a feature flag gated by tenant tier and an emergency fall-back to slab-only behavior.

Relevant links and references:
- See linked Confluence page for telemetry schema and historical kv-cache dashboards.
- Prior art: Facebook "memcached allocator" papers on fragmentation mitigation; net effect is similar but our fused arena needs to be NUMA aware.
